clue.text: Like someone who has yet to think of exploiting contacts?

definitions.text: Like someone who has yet to think of exploiting contacts?

parts.words: Like someone who has yet to think of exploiting contacts
parts.note: contacts are lenses worn on the eye; someone who has not yet switched to them still wears glasses

explanation.surface: A networker who has never thought to use the people they know for advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contacts' reads as business acquaintances; here it means contact lenses, and the person who has not taken them up is still in glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing glasses is described by this adjective, and glasses are what contact lenses replace.

clue.text: Beautiful woman carrying a gun? It's just a game

indicators.note: the woman holds the next pieces within her, so her letters wrap around them

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
gat is old US slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A glamorous woman armed with a pistol insists it is all only play.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a table game played with balls and pins, and the word also means a trifle, something of little importance.

clue.text: Ennobled politician — one for sharpening the knives?

explanation.surface: A peer from politics is cast as the one who whets the blades for a party plot.
explanation.walkthrough: David Steel, former leader of the UK Liberal Party, became Lord Steel; a steel is also the ridged rod used to hone kitchen knives.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord David Steel is a British politician raised to the peerage, and a sharpening rod for blades is called a steel.

clue.text: Little man in endless whirls

indicators.note: the word for whirls loses its final letter, so it no longer has its end

parts.note: eddies are swirls of water or air

explanation.surface: A small person caught up in a ceaseless spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little man' is a short form of a man's name: Eddie is the pet form of Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: A diminutive of Edward or Edwin, so a pet name for a man.

clue.text: Change coaches but with one leaving behind schedule

indicators.note: one of the letters departs from the word for coaches, so it is taken out

parts.note: trains are made up of coaches, and to coach is to train
I is the Roman numeral for one
late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: Rail passengers switching coaches find one service running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes I (one) out of TRAINS to leave TRANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To translate is to render into another language, so to convert or alter something's form.

clue.text: Got together before a match perhaps

definitions.text: Got together before a match perhaps

parts.words: Got together before a match perhaps
parts.note: a match here is a marriage, and a couple who got together beforehand lived as partners without being wed

explanation.surface: Players met up ahead of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests a sporting fixture; it is a wedding, and the couple shared a home before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmarried partners sharing a home are said to have lived together in this way.

clue.text: Old lover on French isle, a banished person

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
île is the French word for island

explanation.surface: A former partner living on an island off France, sent away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sent away from their homeland and forbidden to return is an outcast of this kind.

clue.text: Male at match, I get confused by numbers

indicators.note: the letters of these words are muddled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A man at a sports fixture admits that figures baffle him.
explanation.definitionFit: Done by numbers means calculated with figures, which is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: Fish for a point of view

explanation.surface: Going fishing as a way of seeing things.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with rod and line; an angle is also a particular viewpoint or slant on something.

clue.text: The last hope?

parts.note: the last thing someone might long for is their own end, a desire to die

explanation.surface: Someone's final remaining chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last hope' reads as a final chance; read literally it is a hope for one's last moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A desire to die, conscious or not, is a hope whose object is the end of life.

clue.text: A hill drawn as a new or old boundary

indicators.note: the letters are made new by being put in a different order

explanation.surface: A hill sketched on a map to serve as a border, whether fresh or ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: HADRIAN'S WALL is the Roman wall across northern England, once the empire's frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor's stone wall marked the northern frontier of Britannia, an ancient border line.

clue.text: They manage the accommodation — others lie around

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into another order

explanation.surface: Those who run the lodgings say the rest are lounging about.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotel owners and managers run places where guests stay.

clue.text: Whisky not single malt? Give way, having drunk litre

indicators.note: the first word swallows the next, taking its letter inside

parts.note: to bend is to yield or give way

explanation.surface: A drinker gives in after downing a litre of whisky that is not a single malt.
explanation.definitionFit: A blended whisky mixes malts and grain spirits, unlike a single malt from one distillery.

clue.text: Philosopher terribly inane for many many years

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was a British philosopher

indicators.note: the word is badly jumbled into a different order

explanation.surface: A thinker who has been dreadfully foolish for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: A millennium is a thousand years, so the plural covers a vast span of time.

clue.text: Say, I ache badly! Then start to relax in this?

definitions.text: Say, I ache badly! Then start to relax in this?

indicators.note: these words are badly arranged, so their letters are shuffled
the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A sufferer moans about aches and then sinks into a comfortable seat to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft upholstered armchair is just where an aching person would sink down to rest.

clue.text: Fair one lambasted America as 'very wicked'

indicators.note: the words are beaten up, so their letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A just person has harshly attacked the United States as evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious describes villainous or criminal conduct, extreme wrongdoing.

clue.text: An office worker one rates

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A clerk on short contract assesses things.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi is the plural of tempo, the speed at which music is played.

clue.text: Mother wants jewellery ahead of son? Such may be hard to hear!

definitions.text: Such may be hard to hear!

indicators.note: the jewellery comes before the son in the answer

parts.note: mum is a British word for mother
bling is showy jewellery
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: Mum wants jewels before her boy gets anything, and grumbles about it.
explanation.walkthrough: MUM is the British form of mom.
explanation.definitionFit: Muttered, indistinct words are difficult for listeners to catch.

clue.text: Lock with force beginning to give way

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for force yields and is taken away

parts.note: stress is a force applied to something

explanation.surface: A lock breaks when pressure makes it start to yield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door; it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock or curl of hair.

clue.text: Cricketer misled fan unfairly

indicators.note: the letters are treated unfairly, ending up out of order

explanation.surface: A player deceived a supporter by cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the fielding side tries to stop runs and catch the batter out.
explanation.definitionFit: A player on the fielding side in cricket, positioned to stop or catch the ball.

clue.text: Firm with male in charge like a clown

parts.note: Co. is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company led by a man who behaves foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic means funny or laughable, as a clown's antics are.

clue.text: Creature has nothing to think about

indicators.note: the word for think goes about the next letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to muse is to think or ponder
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An animal with nothing on its mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouse is a small rodent, one kind of animal.

clue.text: Rugby stars fault code for civilised behaviour

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
Leo is a constellation, a group of stars
a flaw is a fault

explanation.surface: Rugby's big names criticise the game's rule book.
explanation.definitionFit: The principle that everyone is bound by the laws is the basis of an orderly society.

clue.text: Bed always tucked in both sides

indicators.note: the word for always is placed inside the letters for both sides

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, both sides
aye is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A bed that is always made with sheets tucked in on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' suggests sleeping; it is a stratum, as in a bed of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed in geology is a stratum, one level of rock or soil.

clue.text: Like some meal that's acceptable, consumed inside

indicators.note: the word for consumed goes within the word for acceptable

parts.note: on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A dish that is fine to eat and has been eaten indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meal' suggests dinner; it is ground grain, as in oatmeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is ground from oats, so it is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Praising a politician for following the archbishop

indicators.note: the politician comes after the archbishop in the answer

parts.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A Conservative lauding a churchman whose lead he follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudatory means expressing praise or commendation.

clue.text: In Brighton a lot like music

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A great deal of Brighton feels like a song.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is an English seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonal relates to tones or keys, a quality of musical sound.

clue.text: This stranger has stirred the deepest affections

indicators.note: these words are stirred up so their letters change order

explanation.surface: An unknown person has moved someone to love.
explanation.walkthrough: Tugging at someone's heartstrings means moving their deepest feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartstrings are one's innermost feelings of love and compassion.
